3. Platinum Rewards Card: Rebate Eligibility and Calcluation
   ID: doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_010
   Score: 12.7250
   Content: ## Eligibility for the Annual Fee Rebate

- The Platinum Rewards Card annual fee rebate is earned only if you meet the required monthly spending threshold in every month of your cardmember year.
- A single month below the threshold disqualifies you from receiving the rebate for that entire cardmember year; there is no partial or prorated rebate.
- If your first cardmember year’s annual fee is waived under a promotional offer, the rebate does not apply to that year. Eligibility begins with the next cardmember year in which the annual fee is billed.

## How the Monthly Calculation Window Works

- Start date: Your first monthly window begins on your account opening date.
- Refresh cadence: Each new monthly window begins on the same calendar day each month (the monthly anniversary of your account opening) and ends the day before the next monthly anniversary.
- Cardmember year: Your rebate evaluation covers 12 consecutive monthly windows, starting from your account opening date (or from the start of the first fee-billed cardmember year after any promotional waiver).
- Posting date rule: Only transactions that post within a given monthly window count toward that month’s threshold. Authorization dates do not control eligibility.

### Example timeline (no amounts)
- Account opened on the 15th:
  - Month 1 window: 15th to the 14th (inclusive by posting date)
  - Month 2 window: 15th to the 14th
  - …
  - Month 12 window: 15th to the 14th
- You must meet the monthly threshold in all 12 windows to earn the rebate for that cardmember year.

## What Counts Toward the Monthly Threshold

Included
- Net purchases posted to your Platinum Rewards Card, including purchases made by authorized users.
- Purchases made using virtual card numbers associated with your account (counted the same as your physical card).
- International purchases, provided they post as purchases.

Excluded
- Fees, interest charges, and adjustments.
- Cash advances and cash-equivalent transactions (for example, money orders, traveler’s checks, and similar cash-like activity).
- Balance transfers.
- Person-to-person money transfers and funding transactions that are coded as cash equivalents.
- Disputed transactions while unresolved.

Adjustments
- Returns, refunds, or credits reduce the monthly total in the window in which the credit posts. A return that posts in a later month can cause you to miss the threshold for that later month.
- Merchant delays can affect posting dates; only posted transactions inside the window count.

## Evaluation and Rebate Posting

- Eligibility is assessed after the close of your 12th monthly window in the cardmember year.
- If you qualified, the rebate is applied as a statement credit to your Platinum Rewards Card account after the annual fee for that cardmember year is billed.
- If the account is closed or product-changed before the year-end evaluation or rebate posting, the rebate will not be awarded.

## Practical Tips

- Track posted transactions by your monthly anniversary dates, not by statement cycle or calendar month.
- Leave a buffer above the monthly threshold to account for late postings or potential returns.
- Confirm that authorized user and virtual card purchases have posted before the monthly window closes.

4. Platinum Reserve Account: Business Credit Card APY Bonuses
   ID: doc_business_savings_accounts_platinum_reserve_account_010
   Score: 12.1099
   Content: ## Eligible Business Credit Cards and APY Bonuses

Holding an eligible Rho-Bank Business Rewards Card can increase the APY on your Platinum Reserve Account. The increase is additive to your current APY and is reflected in your displayed rate and daily interest accruals.

- Business Silver Rewards Card: adds 0.25% to your APY
- Business Gold Rewards Card: adds 0.5% to your APY
- Business Platinum Rewards Card: adds 0.8% to your APY

## How the APY Bonus Is Applied

- The bonus is added as a fixed number of percentage points to your Platinum Reserve Account’s APY based on your eligible card tier.
- The bonus is included in your total APY and affects interest that accrues daily and credits on your normal interest crediting schedule.
- The bonus applies only for the period during which you are eligible; if eligibility begins or ends mid-cycle, the APY used for daily accruals adjusts as of the effective date of that change.

## Verifying Your Bonus

- Check the APY shown in your Platinum Reserve Account details; the increase from your eligible card will be included in the displayed APY.
- Your interest activity will reflect the higher daily accrual associated with the bonus.
- If you hold more than one eligible card or have recently changed cards, contact your Rho-Bank representative to confirm which bonus is currently applied.

## Maintaining Eligibility

To keep the APY bonus active:
- Ensure the eligible Business Rewards Card remains active and in good standing.
- Keep the card associated with the same business entity that owns the Platinum Reserve Account.
- Notify Rho-Bank promptly if your business ownership structure or card status changes, so your APY can be updated accordingly.

## Starting, Changing, or Removing a Bonus

- New or upgraded card: Once eligibility is confirmed, your APY will reflect the applicable bonus going forward.
- Card downgrade, closure, or ineligibility: The APY bonus will no longer apply from the effective date of the change.
- Multiple cards: If your organization holds multiple eligible cards, your account will reflect the applicable bonus for your configuration; contact your Rho-Bank representative if you need confirmation.

## Example (for illustration only)

- If your Platinum Reserve Account APY is 3.00% and you hold a Business Platinum Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.8% to 3.80%.
- If your APY is 2.75% and you hold a Business Gold Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.5% to 3.25%.
- If your APY is 2.25% and you hold a Business Silver Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.25% to 2.50%.

5. Silver Account: Platinum Rewards Card holder benefits
   ID: doc_savings_accounts_silver_account_009
   Score: 12.0362
   Content: ## Overview

Silver Account holders who also have a Platinum Rewards Card receive enhanced withdrawal privileges. Your monthly withdrawal limit is increased by 5 additional free withdrawals, bringing your total to 10 + 5 = 15 withdrawals per month. This benefit is automatically applied when both accounts are linked under the same customer profile. Combined with the existing 15 ATM fee rebates and 0.025% relationship bonus, Platinum Rewards Card holders get an elevated Silver Account experience.

## APY bonuses from credit cards
- Platinum Rewards Card: +0.2%
- Diamond Elite Card: +0.25%

## What you receive as a Platinum Rewards Card holder

- Additional free withdrawals: +5 per month on top of your standard 10 free withdrawals
- Total free withdrawals per month: 10 + 5 = 15
- ATM fee relief: Up to 15 in ATM fee rebates each month
- Earnings boost: An additional 0.025% relationship bonus added to your APY when eligible

## Activation and eligibility

- The enhanced withdrawal limit is automatically applied when your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card are linked under the same customer profile.
- The 0.025% relationship bonus and 15 ATM fee rebates apply in the same profile-linked setup.

### How to confirm your accounts are linked

1. Sign in to Rho-Bank Online Banking or the mobile app.
2. Open your customer profile and review your list of accounts and cards.
3. Verify that your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card appear under the same customer profile.
4. If you do not see both products under one profile, consolidate them to a single profile or contact us for assistance.

## Using your monthly withdrawal allowance

- Counting method: Any transaction classified as a withdrawal under your Silver Account terms counts toward your monthly total of 15 free withdrawals.
- Cycle timing: Your free withdrawal count resets at the start of each monthly statement cycle.
- Beyond the limit: Transactions above your free monthly total may be subject to standard Silver Account withdrawal charges.

Example:
- You make 12 withdrawals in a month: all 12 are free.
- You make 15 withdrawals in a month: all 15 are free.
- You make 16 withdrawals in a month: the first 15 are free; the 16th may incur standard charges.

## ATM fee rebates

- You are eligible for up to 15 in ATM fee rebates each month.
- Rebates apply after ATM fees post to your Silver Account; check your transaction history for the corresponding credit within the same month.

## Relationship bonus APY

- When your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card are linked under the same customer profile, an additional 0.025% is added to your APY as a relationship bonus.
- The relationship bonus is reflected in your APY while eligibility is maintained.

## Troubleshooting and tips

- If you do not see the extra withdrawals or 0.025% reflected, confirm both products are under the same customer profile.
- Check that you are within the current monthly statement cycle for the added withdrawals to apply.
- Review your transaction history to verify ATM fee charges and corresponding rebates up to 15 for the month.

1. How can I close a credit card account?
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_001
   Score: 22.2001
   Content: ## Eligibility Requirements for Account Closure

To close your Rho-Bank credit card account, you must meet all of the following:

1. Zero balance required: Your account must have an outstanding balance of $0.00 dollars. Wait for any pending transactions to post, then pay the full statement balance.
2. No pending disputes: Accounts with active or pending transaction disputes cannot be closed (pending disputes allowed: No). Request closure only after all disputes are fully resolved.

Closing a credit card may affect your credit score by reducing your total available credit and potentially impacting your credit utilization ratio. This impact can be more significant if the card has a high credit limit or is among your oldest accounts.

All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer. For example, a $126.77 purchase on a 1% cash back card earns 126 points (not 127), because 126.77 × 0.01 = 1.2677 points, which rounds down to 1 point per dollar, giving 126 points. Similarly, a $99.99 purchase at 2.5% cash back would calculate to 249.975 points but would award 249 points. This rounding policy applies consistently across all credit card types and reward categories.

   Content: At Rho-Bank, we want to make sure you receive every dollar of cash back that you've earned. You might want to contact us about your cash back if:

- A purchase that should have earned bonus cash back only received the standard rate
- You made a purchase in a bonus category but didn't receive the higher reward rate
- The cash back amount seems lower than what you calculated based on your card's rates
- A qualifying purchase doesn't show any rewards at all
- You believe a merchant was miscategorized and you should have earned a different rate

## How We Can Help

Our customer service team has the tools to investigate cash back discrepancies and review your transaction history. When you contact us, we'll look into the specific transaction, verify the merchant category, check the applicable reward rates for your card, and determine if an adjustment is needed. If we find that you were indeed shortchanged on your rewards, we'll make sure the correct amount is applied to your account.

## What You'll Need

- The date of the transaction in question
- The merchant name and purchase amount
- The cash back amount you received versus what you expected
- Any receipts or documentation you have from the purchase

## Contact Us

If you think you're missing cash back or have any questions about how your rewards are calculated, please reach out to our customer service team. You can call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK, chat with us through the Rho-Bank mobile app, or visit rhobank.com/help. We're committed to ensuring you get the full value of your Rho-Bank credit card rewards.

4. Silver Account: Platinum Rewards Card holder benefits
   ID: doc_savings_accounts_silver_account_009
   Score: 15.5718
   Content: ## Overview

Silver Account holders who also have a Platinum Rewards Card receive enhanced withdrawal privileges. Your monthly withdrawal limit is increased by 5 additional free withdrawals, bringing your total to 10 + 5 = 15 withdrawals per month. This benefit is automatically applied when both accounts are linked under the same customer profile. Combined with the existing 15 ATM fee rebates and 0.025% relationship bonus, Platinum Rewards Card holders get an elevated Silver Account experience.

## APY bonuses from credit cards
- Platinum Rewards Card: +0.2%
- Diamond Elite Card: +0.25%

## What you receive as a Platinum Rewards Card holder

- Additional free withdrawals: +5 per month on top of your standard 10 free withdrawals
- Total free withdrawals per month: 10 + 5 = 15
- ATM fee relief: Up to 15 in ATM fee rebates each month
- Earnings boost: An additional 0.025% relationship bonus added to your APY when eligible

## Activation and eligibility

- The enhanced withdrawal limit is automatically applied when your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card are linked under the same customer profile.
- The 0.025% relationship bonus and 15 ATM fee rebates apply in the same profile-linked setup.

### How to confirm your accounts are linked

1. Sign in to Rho-Bank Online Banking or the mobile app.
2. Open your customer profile and review your list of accounts and cards.
3. Verify that your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card appear under the same customer profile.
4. If you do not see both products under one profile, consolidate them to a single profile or contact us for assistance.

## Using your monthly withdrawal allowance

- Counting method: Any transaction classified as a withdrawal under your Silver Account terms counts toward your monthly total of 15 free withdrawals.
- Cycle timing: Your free withdrawal count resets at the start of each monthly statement cycle.
- Beyond the limit: Transactions above your free monthly total may be subject to standard Silver Account withdrawal charges.

Example:
- You make 12 withdrawals in a month: all 12 are free.
- You make 15 withdrawals in a month: all 15 are free.
- You make 16 withdrawals in a month: the first 15 are free; the 16th may incur standard charges.

## ATM fee rebates

- You are eligible for up to 15 in ATM fee rebates each month.
- Rebates apply after ATM fees post to your Silver Account; check your transaction history for the corresponding credit within the same month.

## Relationship bonus APY

- When your Silver Account and Platinum Rewards Card are linked under the same customer profile, an additional 0.025% is added to your APY as a relationship bonus.
- The relationship bonus is reflected in your APY while eligibility is maintained.

## Troubleshooting and tips

- If you do not see the extra withdrawals or 0.025% reflected, confirm both products are under the same customer profile.
- Check that you are within the current monthly statement cycle for the added withdrawals to apply.
- Review your transaction history to verify ATM fee charges and corresponding rebates up to 15 for the month.

8. Platinum Reserve Account: Business Credit Card APY Bonuses
   ID: doc_business_savings_accounts_platinum_reserve_account_010
   Score: 14.2992
   Content: ## Eligible Business Credit Cards and APY Bonuses

Holding an eligible Rho-Bank Business Rewards Card can increase the APY on your Platinum Reserve Account. The increase is additive to your current APY and is reflected in your displayed rate and daily interest accruals.

- Business Silver Rewards Card: adds 0.25% to your APY
- Business Gold Rewards Card: adds 0.5% to your APY
- Business Platinum Rewards Card: adds 0.8% to your APY

## How the APY Bonus Is Applied

- The bonus is added as a fixed number of percentage points to your Platinum Reserve Account’s APY based on your eligible card tier.
- The bonus is included in your total APY and affects interest that accrues daily and credits on your normal interest crediting schedule.
- The bonus applies only for the period during which you are eligible; if eligibility begins or ends mid-cycle, the APY used for daily accruals adjusts as of the effective date of that change.

## Verifying Your Bonus

- Check the APY shown in your Platinum Reserve Account details; the increase from your eligible card will be included in the displayed APY.
- Your interest activity will reflect the higher daily accrual associated with the bonus.
- If you hold more than one eligible card or have recently changed cards, contact your Rho-Bank representative to confirm which bonus is currently applied.

## Maintaining Eligibility

To keep the APY bonus active:
- Ensure the eligible Business Rewards Card remains active and in good standing.
- Keep the card associated with the same business entity that owns the Platinum Reserve Account.
- Notify Rho-Bank promptly if your business ownership structure or card status changes, so your APY can be updated accordingly.

## Starting, Changing, or Removing a Bonus

- New or upgraded card: Once eligibility is confirmed, your APY will reflect the applicable bonus going forward.
- Card downgrade, closure, or ineligibility: The APY bonus will no longer apply from the effective date of the change.
- Multiple cards: If your organization holds multiple eligible cards, your account will reflect the applicable bonus for your configuration; contact your Rho-Bank representative if you need confirmation.

## Example (for illustration only)

- If your Platinum Reserve Account APY is 3.00% and you hold a Business Platinum Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.8% to 3.80%.
- If your APY is 2.75% and you hold a Business Gold Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.5% to 3.25%.
- If your APY is 2.25% and you hold a Business Silver Rewards Card, your APY would increase by 0.25% to 2.50%.

10. How can I close a credit card account?
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_001
   Score: 13.9196
   Content: ## Eligibility Requirements for Account Closure

To close your Rho-Bank credit card account, you must meet all of the following:

1. Zero balance required: Your account must have an outstanding balance of $0.00 dollars. Wait for any pending transactions to post, then pay the full statement balance.
2. No pending disputes: Accounts with active or pending transaction disputes cannot be closed (pending disputes allowed: No). Request closure only after all disputes are fully resolved.
3. Minimum account age: Your account must have been open for at least 60 days.
4. No pending replacement cards: If a replacement card has been ordered and not yet received or activated, complete or cancel the replacement process before requesting closure.

## Rewards and Annual Fee Policies

- Unredeemed rewards: You have 45 days after submitting your closure request to redeem any remaining rewards. After this period, all unredeemed rewards are permanently forfeited.
- Annual fee refund: If you close your account within 37 days of the annual fee posting, you are eligible for a full refund of that fee. After this window, no refund is provided.

## Impact on Credit Score

Closing a credit card may affect your credit score by reducing your total available credit and potentially impacting your credit utilization ratio. This impact can be more significant if the card has a high credit limit or is among your oldest accounts.

   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_019

   Content: One of the great benefits of your Rho-Bank credit card is the ability to earn rewards on your everyday purchases. To help you maximize your earnings, it's important to understand how reward categories work and which types of purchases qualify for bonus rewards on your specific card.

## How Reward Categories Work

Every Rho-Bank credit card earns rewards on all purchases, but certain categories of spending may earn you bonus rewards at a higher rate. Your card has a base reward rate that applies to all purchases, plus bonus categories where you can earn even more. The specific bonus categories and rates vary depending on which Rho-Bank credit card you have.

## Available Reward Categories

Rho-Bank recognizes the following spending categories for rewards purposes:

- **Travel**: Flights, hotels, car rentals, cruises, and other travel-related purchases
- **Dining**: Restaurants, cafes, bars, and food delivery services
- **Groceries**: Supermarkets, grocery stores, and specialty food shops
- **Entertainment**: Movies, concerts, sporting events, and streaming services
- **Shopping**: Retail stores, department stores, and online marketplaces
- **Utilities**: Electric, gas, water, internet, and phone bills
- **Transportation**: Rideshare services, public transit, parking, and tolls
- **Software**: Software subscriptions, licenses, and cloud services
- **Media**: Advertising spend and digital media purchases
- **Green/Sustainable**: Eco-friendly merchants and sustainable products
- **Operations**: Business operational expenses

## Maximizing Your Rewards

To get the most out of your rewards, we recommend using your Rho-Bank credit card for purchases in your card's bonus categories whenever possible. You can find your specific card's bonus categories and reward rates by logging into your account on the Rho-Bank mobile app or website, or by reviewing your card's terms and conditions.

If you have any questions about which category a particular merchant falls into, or how to maximize your rewards earning potential, our customer service team is always happy to help. Give us a call at 1-800-RHO-BANK or chat with us through the mobile app.

   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021

   Content: At Rho-Bank, we want to make sure you receive every dollar of cash back that you've earned. We understand that occasionally there may be discrepancies between the cash back you expected to receive on a purchase and what actually appeared on your account. If you've reviewed your rewards and something doesn't seem right, we're here to help investigate and make it right.

## When to Reach Out

You might want to contact us about your cash back if:

- A purchase that should have earned bonus cash back only received the standard rate
- You made a purchase in a bonus category but didn't receive the higher reward rate
- The cash back amount seems lower than what you calculated based on your card's rates
- A qualifying purchase doesn't show any rewards at all
- You believe a merchant was miscategorized and you should have earned a different rate

## How We Can Help

Our customer service team has the tools to investigate cash back discrepancies and review your transaction history. When you contact us, we'll look into the specific transaction, verify the merchant category, check the applicable reward rates for your card, and determine if an adjustment is needed. If we find that you were indeed shortchanged on your rewards, we'll make sure the correct amount is applied to your account.

## What You'll Need

To help us investigate quickly, it's helpful to have the following information ready when you contact us:

- The date of the transaction in question
- The merchant name and purchase amount
- The cash back amount you received versus what you expected
- Any receipts or documentation you have from the purchase

## Contact Us

If you think you're missing cash back or have any questions about how your rewards are calculated, please reach out to our customer service team. You can call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK, chat with us through the Rho-Bank mobile app, or visit rhobank.com/help. We're committed to ensuring you get the full value of your Rho-Bank credit card rewards.

9. Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines (Internal)
   ID: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015
   Score: 18.3260
   Content: ## Overview
When processing a credit card transaction dispute, you must determine whether the customer is eligible for provisional credit. Provisional credit means the disputed amount is temporarily credited back to the customer's account while the investigation is ongoing.

## Eligibility Criteria — Customer is ELIGIBLE for provisional credit if ALL of the following are true:
1. Account Standing: The customer's credit card account has been open for at least 60 days
2. Dispute Reason Category: The dispute reason is one of the following:
   - 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge'
   - 'duplicate_charge'
   - 'goods_services_not_received' (only if purchase was made more than 30 days ago)
3. Dispute Amount: The transaction amount must be at least $25.00 and must not exceed the card's maximum provisional credit limit based on card tier (see below)
4. Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months
5. Contacted Merchant: For non-fraud disputes (anything other than 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge'), the customer must have attempted to resolve with the merchant first

## Maximum Provisional Credit Limits by Card Tier
- Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): Maximum $2500.00
- Mid Tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): Maximum $5000.00
- Premium Tier (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card): Maximum $10000.00
- Elite Tier (Platinum Rewards Card, Business Platinum Rewards Card): Maximum $15000.00
- Invitation Tier (Diamond Elite Card): Maximum $25000.00

## NOT Eligible Scenarios
- Account is less than 60 days old
- Dispute reason is 'incorrect_amount', 'goods_services_not_as_described', 'canceled_subscription_still_charging', or 'refund_never_processed'
- Transaction amount is under $25.00 or exceeds the card's maximum limit based on tier
- For non-fraud disputes: customer did not contact merchant first
- 'goods_services_not_received' where purchase was made within the last 30 days (merchant may still be processing delivery)

10. Platinum Rewards Card: Rebate Eligibility and Calcluation
   ID: doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_010
   Score: 18.1586
   Content: ## Eligibility for the Annual Fee Rebate

- The Platinum Rewards Card annual fee rebate is earned only if you meet the required monthly spending threshold in every month of your cardmember year.
- A single month below the threshold disqualifies you from receiving the rebate for that entire cardmember year; there is no partial or prorated rebate.
- If your first cardmember year’s annual fee is waived under a promotional offer, the rebate does not apply to that year. Eligibility begins with the next cardmember year in which the annual fee is billed.

## How the Monthly Calculation Window Works

- Start date: Your first monthly window begins on your account opening date.
- Refresh cadence: Each new monthly window begins on the same calendar day each month (the monthly anniversary of your account opening) and ends the day before the next monthly anniversary.
- Cardmember year: Your rebate evaluation covers 12 consecutive monthly windows, starting from your account opening date (or from the start of the first fee-billed cardmember year after any promotional waiver).
- Posting date rule: Only transactions that post within a given monthly window count toward that month’s threshold. Authorization dates do not control eligibility.

### Example timeline (no amounts)
- Account opened on the 15th:
  - Month 1 window: 15th to the 14th (inclusive by posting date)
  - Month 2 window: 15th to the 14th
  - …
  - Month 12 window: 15th to the 14th
- You must meet the monthly threshold in all 12 windows to earn the rebate for that cardmember year.

## What Counts Toward the Monthly Threshold

Included
- Net purchases posted to your Platinum Rewards Card, including purchases made by authorized users.
- Purchases made using virtual card numbers associated with your account (counted the same as your physical card).
- International purchases, provided they post as purchases.

Excluded
- Fees, interest charges, and adjustments.
- Cash advances and cash-equivalent transactions (for example, money orders, traveler’s checks, and similar cash-like activity).
- Balance transfers.
- Person-to-person money transfers and funding transactions that are coded as cash equivalents.
- Disputed transactions while unresolved.

Adjustments
- Returns, refunds, or credits reduce the monthly total in the window in which the credit posts. A return that posts in a later month can cause you to miss the threshold for that later month.
- Merchant delays can affect posting dates; only posted transactions inside the window count.

## Evaluation and Rebate Posting

- Eligibility is assessed after the close of your 12th monthly window in the cardmember year.
- If you qualified, the rebate is applied as a statement credit to your Platinum Rewards Card account after the annual fee for that cardmember year is billed.
- If the account is closed or product-changed before the year-end evaluation or rebate posting, the rebate will not be awarded.

## Practical Tips

- Track posted transactions by your monthly anniversary dates, not by statement cycle or calendar month.
- Leave a buffer above the monthly threshold to account for late postings or potential returns.
- Confirm that authorized user and virtual card purchases have posted before the monthly window closes.

# Rho-Bank Customer Service Policy

You are a helpful customer service agent for Rho-Bank.
Your goal is to help customers by searching the knowledge base and providing accurate information.

## Guidelines

1. Do not make up policies, information or actions that you can take on behalf of the user. All instructions will be found here or in the knowledge base. If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know. 
2. Do not ask for any documentation, receipts... from the customer unless it states very clearly in the knowledge base how to process it, and whether you're allowed to do so. 
3. Be polite and professional
4. If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool. Do not make up or assume the current time. 
5. Generally, if the issue cannot be resolved or is outside your capabilities, ask the user whether they would like to be transferred to a human agent. If they do, invoke the appropriate transfer_to_human_agents tool. Do this only if you absolutely have to, and you are sure that there are no potential actions you can take as specified in the knowledge base, or in your policy. Do not transfer without asking the user first. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
6. If an issue falls within your capabilities and the user still wants to be transferred to a human agent, kindly inform the user that you can help them, and try to help them first. If the user asks for a human agent 4 times, then you may invoke the transfer_to_human_agents tool. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
7. Do not give intermediate responses to users while processing that would give away internal rho-bank information/policies. 


**Search the knowledge base** for relevant information when appropriate using the provided `KB_search` tool (uses BM25 for retrieval).


## Additional Instructions

### Discoverable Tools

#### Giving Discoverable Tools to Users
The knowledge base may contain instructions that indicate certain actions should be performed by the user themselves rather than by you. These are called "user discoverable tools." A user discoverable tool is a tool that you provide to the user so they can execute it on their own (e.g., through a customer portal or app).

**When to give user discoverable tools:**
-  Only give a tool when the user would like to perform an action, and the knowledge base explicitly has a tool that allows the user to perform this action (e.g., "to do X, have the user call tool_name(args)"). IMPORTANT: Do not unlock tools that you do not plan on giving to the user and actually using: this causes issues in database logging.
- You must search the knowledge base to find tools that you can give. Do not invent or guess user discoverable tools 
- Only use tool names and arguments discovered in the knowledge base

**How to give a tool:**
- Use the `give_discoverable_user_tool(discoverable_tool_name)` function
- Provide the exact tool name  as specified in the knowledge base
- Explain to the user what the tool does and how to use it, and what arguments to provide. Just explaining isn't enough, you must use the `give_discoverable_user_tool(discoverable_tool_name)` function.

#### Unlocking and Using Agent Discoverable Tools
The knowledge base may contain references to specialized internal tools that you can unlock and use. These are called "agent discoverable tools." Unlike regular tools which are always available, these tools must be explicitly unlocked after discovering them in the knowledge base.

**When to use agent discoverable tools:**
- Only unlock a tool when the knowledge base explicitly mentions it (e.g., "use tool_name to perform X"), and do not unlock tools you do not plan to use.
- You must search the knowledge base to find tools that you can unlock. Do not invent or guess tool names - only use tool names discovered in the knowledge base.

**How to use agent discoverable tools:**
1. First, unlock the tool using `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool(agent_tool_name)` with the exact tool name from the knowledge base: you must unlock the tool before using it to get information on the proper params. IMPORTANT: Do not unlock tools that you do not plan on actually using: this causes issues in database logging.
2. Then, call the tool using `call_discoverable_agent_tool(agent_tool_name, arguments)` with the required arguments
3. The unlock step is required before calling - you cannot call a tool that hasn't been unlocked

### Authenticating Users

Generally, for any scenario involving accessing customer information in internal databases, you must first verify their identify before proceeding. No need to verify more than once in a single conversation. You should ONLY verify a user's identity if you need to access or modify their customer information in internal databases on their behalf.

Here are some concrete examples:
* Looking up account balances, transaction history, referral history...
* Changing account settings (e.g., address, phone number, email)
* Closing an account
* Adding or removing authorized users
* Requesting information about specific transactions
* Discussing specific loan or credit details
* Filing a dispute on behalf of the user

To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address. Knowing full name or userID is not enough to verify. After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records. Do not leak any information about the user before they are verified.

1. No foreign transaction fees explained
   ID: doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_003
   Score: 19.9935
   Content: ## What this means for you
- Purchases and withdrawals in a non‑USD currency do not incur a foreign transaction fee. Your rate is 0% for foreign currency transactions.

## Where this applies
- Card purchases processed in a foreign currency
- Online transactions charged in a foreign currency
- International ATM withdrawals, as they relate to the foreign transaction fee

## What is not included
- Local ATM operator surcharges and network fees are separate from the foreign transaction fee policy.
- Check-related services are not part of foreign transaction fees. For example, placing a stop payment carries a fee of $25.

### Tips
- If a merchant offers to charge you in USD rather than the local currency, that is a separate service and may have its own costs set by the merchant or processor.

2. World Blue: Free International ATM Access
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_world_blue_009
   Score: 19.8181
   Content: ## What you pay at foreign ATMs

- Rho foreign ATM withdrawal fee: 0% (minimum $0.00)
- Foreign ATM fee rebates: Up to $100 per calendar month for fees charged by foreign ATM operators on cash withdrawals

You will not be charged a Rho fee for international ATM withdrawals. If the foreign ATM operator adds its own fee, we rebate those fees automatically up to the monthly cap.

### Snapshot of foreign ATM costs
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Rho foreign ATM withdrawal fee | 0% |
| Rho foreign ATM withdrawal fee minimum | $0.00 |
| Maximum monthly rebate for foreign ATM fees | $100 |

## Monthly rebate rules

- Coverage: Rebates apply to fees assessed by foreign ATM operators on cash withdrawals.
- Cap: We rebate up to a total of $100 in a calendar month. Fees above this amount will not be reimbursed for that month.
- Posting: Rebates are issued automatically after the withdrawal and associated fee post to your account. No enrollment or receipt submission is required.

Tip: Keep your ATM receipt when a foreign ATM displays or charges a fee; it’s useful for reference if you need to follow up.

## How to make a fee-free withdrawal abroad

1. Use your card at an international ATM that accepts it.
2. When prompted, select a withdrawal from checking.
3. If asked about currency choice, choose to be charged in the local currency rather than having the ATM convert the amount.
4. Complete your withdrawal. If the ATM charges a fee, it will typically display it before you confirm.

## Example

- You withdraw the equivalent of $200 at a foreign ATM.
- Rho foreign ATM withdrawal fee: 0% with a $0.00 minimum, so you pay $0 to Rho.
- The ATM operator charges a $5 fee. We automatically rebate $5, counting toward your $100 monthly cap.

3. Lime Green Account: ATM Access and Fee Rebates
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_lime_green_007
   Score: 19.6258
   Content: ## ATM Access

- You can use out-of-network ATMs for cash withdrawals. Each out-of-network ATM transaction is assessed a fee of $1.00.
- International (foreign) ATM withdrawals incur a fee equal to 1.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $2.50 per withdrawal.

### Quick reference

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Out-of-network ATM transaction fee (domestic) | $1.00 per transaction |
| Foreign ATM withdrawal fee | 1.5% of amount; minimum $2.50 |
| Monthly ATM fee rebate cap (out-of-network usage) | Up to $25 per month |

## ATM Fee Rebates

- Your account provides monthly rebates of eligible fees from out-of-network ATM usage, up to $25 per month.
- Rebates are applied until the monthly cap is reached; any eligible fees above the cap are your responsibility.
- You do not need to take additional action for eligible rebates—fees and corresponding credits will appear as separate line items on your account activity once processed.

### What counts toward the monthly cap

- Fees assessed for out-of-network ATM usage that are charged to your account are counted toward the $25 monthly rebate limit.

## How fees are calculated

- Domestic out-of-network usage: Each withdrawal is charged $1.00.
- Foreign ATM withdrawals: The fee is 1.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $2.50. If the percentage-based amount is less than $2.50, the $2.50 minimum applies.

## Examples

- Domestic, multiple withdrawals:
  - If you make several out-of-network withdrawals in a month, each is charged $1.00. Eligible out-of-network ATM fees will be rebated up to a total of $25 for that month.

- Foreign withdrawal:
  - For a single international withdrawal, your fee is calculated at 1.5% of the withdrawn amount, subject to a $2.50 minimum. The applicable amount is charged at the time the transaction is processed.

## Tips to reduce fees

- Consolidate cash needs into fewer withdrawals to limit per-transaction charges of $1.00.
- Monitor your monthly total of out-of-network ATM fees to understand how close you are to the $25 rebate cap.

4. Hunter Green Account: ATM Fees and Out-of-Network Usage
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_hunter_green_010
   Score: 19.2479
   Content: ## Fee Summary

- Out-of-network (non‑Rho) ATM transactions (domestic): $2.00 per transaction
- International ATM withdrawals: 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $4.00 per withdrawal
- Monthly ATM fee rebates for out-of-network usage: Up to $20 per month

Note: ATM owner/operator surcharges are set by the ATM and are separate from Rho fees.

## How Fees Apply

### Domestic out-of-network usage
- Each cash withdrawal at a non‑Rho ATM incurs a $2.00 fee.

## Calculating Your Total Cost

For each ATM withdrawal:
1. Add any ATM owner/operator surcharge shown at the terminal.
2. If the ATM is non‑Rho, add $2.00.
3. If the withdrawal is international, add 2.5% of the withdrawal amount (minimum $4.00).
4. Subtract any applicable rebates, up to a total of $20 per month.

## Examples

- Domestic, non‑Rho ATM, $100 withdrawal:
  - Rho out-of-network fee: $2.00

9. Troubleshooting: Hunter Green Fees and Charges
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_hunter_green_009
   Score: 15.8275
   Content: ## Identify and Resolve Unexpected Charges

Use the sections below to diagnose why a fee posted, how it’s calculated, and what to do if you believe it’s incorrect.

---

## Monthly Maintenance Fee

You were charged $25.00 if the account did not meet the waiver criteria for the statement period.

Troubleshooting steps:
- Confirm your statement period and check the “Fees & Charges” section for the $25.00 line.
- Verify whether your balance met the waiver threshold of $5,000 for the period.
- If you recently moved funds near the end of the cycle, the timing of deposits/withdrawals may have affected the period-end balance used to determine the waiver.
- If you believe your balance qualified for the waiver but the fee posted, request a review and include your statement period and balance details for the period.

Tips to avoid future charges:
- Keep your balance at or above $5,000 throughout the statement period.
- Set internal alerts to notify you before the cycle ends if your balance is trending below $5,000.

---

## Domestic Wire Transfer Fee

An outgoing domestic wire triggers a fee of $15.00.

Troubleshooting steps:
- Review your transaction history for outgoing domestic wires on the date the fee posted.
- Check whether a team member initiated a wire or if a scheduled/recurring wire executed.
- If you see multiple fees for a single wire, compare timestamps and reference numbers; submit both entries for review if they appear duplicative.

How to avoid:
- Where possible, consider alternative transfer methods for domestic payments that do not incur the $15.00.

---

## ATM Fees

### Domestic out-of-network ATM usage
- Fee: $2.00 per transaction when using non‑Rho ATMs within the U.S.
- You may also see a separate surcharge from the ATM operator; this is set by the ATM owner.

Troubleshooting steps:
- Match the ATM withdrawal date/time and location to the fee posted.
- If you were using an in-network ATM but still see $2.00, provide the ATM address and receipt for review.

### Foreign (international) ATM withdrawals
- Fee: 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $4.00.
- In addition, the ATM operator may add its own surcharge.

How the fee is calculated:
- The fee is the greater of:
  - Withdrawal amount × 2.5%
  - $4.00

Examples:
- Withdrawing 80.00 in local currency equivalent: 80.00 × 2.5% = 2.00; minimum $4.00 applies, so the fee is $4.00.
- Withdrawing 400.00 in local currency equivalent: 400.00 × 2.5% = 10.00; since this exceeds $4.00, the fee is 10.00.

If a foreign ATM fee looks incorrect:
- Confirm the final settled withdrawal amount (in USD equivalent) used for the percentage calculation.
- Check for any separate ATM-operator surcharge on your receipt.
- If you see both a foreign ATM fee and a domestic out-of-network fee for the same international withdrawal, share the transaction details for review.

---

## Sustainability Allocations Within Fees

Some fees on Hunter Green include a carbon-offset allocation. If you see a note or line item indicating a contribution tied to a fee:
- This does not increase the total you pay beyond the published fee amounts (e.g., $25.00, $15.00, $2.00).
- If you believe a separate charge was added in error rather than noted as an allocation within an existing fee, share the statement line items for review.

---

## Quick Reference: Fees Discussed Here

| Charge type                          | Amount/Calculation |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------|
| Monthly maintenance fee             | $25.00 |
| Waiver threshold (per period)       | $5,000 |
| Domestic wire (outgoing)            | $15.00 |
| Domestic out-of-network ATM         | $2.00 per transaction |
| Foreign ATM withdrawal              | 2.5% (minimum $4.00) |

---

## Requesting a Fee Review

Provide the following to expedite resolution:
- Statement period and the specific fee(s) in question
- For maintenance fee reviews: balance evidence relative to $5,000 during the period
- For domestic wire fees: wire date, amount, and reference
- For ATM fees: date/time, location, receipt (showing any operator surcharge), and the withdrawal amount used to compute the fee

Submit this information through your usual Rho support channel.

10. World Blue: Traveling Abroad with Your Business Account
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_world_blue_005
   Score: 15.7165
   Content: ## Using Your Account Abroad: Cash, Payments, and Controls

Traveling internationally with World Blue is straightforward. The following guidance covers how to access cash, move money, and manage team permissions while you’re on the road.

### Accessing Cash at Foreign ATMs

- You can withdraw local currency abroad without a foreign ATM fee from us.
- Our foreign ATM withdrawal fee is 0% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $0.00.

ATM fee policy summary:
- Rho foreign ATM fee: 0% (minimum $0.00)
- Rebate of ATM operator surcharges: Up to $100 per month

Best practices when withdrawing:
- Choose to be charged in the local currency and decline “dynamic currency conversion” on the ATM to access low‑margin FX rates.
- Prefer bank‑branded ATMs; avoid independent kiosks in tourist areas when possible.
- Keep ATM receipts until your statement closes in case you need to reference fees.
- If multiple employees are traveling, consider setting withdrawal limits and time‑of‑day windows via role permissions.

### Sending and Receiving Payments While Abroad

- You can send and receive cross‑border payments in $140 countries/regions via SWIFT and, where eligible, SEPA.
- Use SEPA for euro‑area beneficiaries when available; use SWIFT for other destinations and currencies.

To send an international payment on the road:
1. Add or select the beneficiary.
2. Choose the payment network (SEPA where eligible, otherwise SWIFT).
3. Select the funding currency from your multi‑currency balances or convert before sending.
4. Enter amount and review the overview screen for currency and network details.
5. Submit and monitor delivery status in your activity feed.

Receiving payments while abroad:
- Share the correct currency‑specific receiving details from your account profile with overseas payers.
- If a payer requests network preference, provide SEPA details for euro payments within the SEPA area; otherwise provide SWIFT details.

### Depositing Funds While Traveling

- Mobile check deposit is available up to $20,000 per day.
- Tips for smooth deposits while abroad:
  - Use clear, well‑lit images on a flat, dark background.
  - Endorse checks as required and include any instructed phrases in the endorsement.
  - Retain the physical check securely until the deposit is confirmed.

### Managing Team Access and Approvals on the Road

Use tiered permissions to keep control while enabling travel flexibility:
- Create a “Travel” role with only the capabilities your travelers need (e.g., ATM withdrawals, card spend, or initiating—but not approving—international wires).
- Set per‑user spend limits and require approvals for high‑value SWIFT payments.
- Restrict who can add new international beneficiaries; require a second approver before first‑time payments.

### Pre‑Trip Checklist

- Confirm each traveler’s ATM PIN and test a small withdrawal before departure.
- Set or review withdrawal and spend limits appropriate for the trip’s costs.
- Pre‑add frequent international beneficiaries and verify their details.
- Ensure the right approvers will be available across time zones for urgent payments.

|---|---|

| Foreign ATM withdrawal fee | 1.5% of amount; minimum $2.50 |

- Your account provides monthly rebates of eligible fees from out-of-network ATM usage, up to $25 per month.
- Rebates are applied until the monthly cap is reached; any eligible fees above the cap are your responsibility.
- You do not need to take additional action for eligible rebates—fees and corresponding credits will appear as separate line items on your account activity once processed.

### What counts toward the monthly cap

- Fees assessed for out-of-network ATM usage that are charged to your account are counted toward the $25 monthly rebate limit.

## How fees are calculated

- Domestic out-of-network usage: Each withdrawal is charged $1.00.

## Monthly rebate rules

8. Hunter Green Account: ATM Fees and Out-of-Network Usage
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_hunter_green_010

   Content: ## Fee Summary

- Out-of-network (non‑Rho) ATM transactions (domestic): $2.00 per transaction
- International ATM withdrawals: 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $4.00 per withdrawal
- Monthly ATM fee rebates for out-of-network usage: Up to $20 per month

Note: ATM owner/operator surcharges are set by the ATM and are separate from Rho fees.

## How Fees Apply

### Domestic out-of-network usage
- Each cash withdrawal at a non‑Rho ATM incurs a $2.00 fee.
- Any surcharge displayed by the ATM owner/operator will be charged in addition to the Rho fee.
- Eligible out-of-network ATM fees are automatically rebated until you reach the monthly cap of $20.

### International ATM withdrawals
- Each withdrawal outside the U.S. incurs a fee of 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum charge of $4.00 per withdrawal.
- If the international withdrawal is made at a non‑Rho ATM, the $2.00 out-of-network fee also applies.
- ATM owner/operator surcharges at foreign ATMs may also be charged.
- Eligible out-of-network ATM fees are rebated up to the monthly maximum of $20.

## Calculating Your Total Cost

For each ATM withdrawal:
1. Add any ATM owner/operator surcharge shown at the terminal.
2. If the ATM is non‑Rho, add $2.00.
3. If the withdrawal is international, add 2.5% of the withdrawal amount (minimum $4.00).
4. Subtract any applicable rebates, up to a total of $20 per month.

## Examples

- Domestic, non‑Rho ATM, $100 withdrawal:
  - Rho out-of-network fee: $2.00
  - Plus any ATM owner surcharge
  - Rebated up to your remaining monthly $20 cap

- International ATM, $100 withdrawal:
  - International fee: 2.5% of $100 = $2.50, but minimum applies → $4.00
  - Out-of-network fee (if the ATM is non‑Rho): $2.00
  - Plus any ATM owner surcharge
  - Rebated up to your remaining monthly $20 cap

- International ATM, $400 withdrawal:
  - International fee: 2.5% of $400 = $10.00
  - Out-of-network fee (if the ATM is non‑Rho): $2.00
  - Plus any ATM owner surcharge
  - Rebated up to your remaining monthly $20 cap

- Out-of-network usage: Any transaction at a non‑Rho ATM is assessed a per‑transaction fee of $2.50.
- International usage: ATM cash withdrawals at foreign (international) ATMs are assessed a fee of 3% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $5.00.
- Operator surcharges: The ATM owner may charge an additional surcharge at the terminal. This surcharge is separate from Rho fees.

## Fee schedule
| Scenario | Fee | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic out‑of‑network ATM transaction | $2.50 per transaction | Applies at non‑Rho ATMs in the U.S. |
| International ATM cash withdrawal | 3% of withdrawal amount (min. $5.00) | Applies at foreign ATMs outside the U.S. |
| Monthly rebates for out‑of‑network usage | Up to $10 per calendar month | Rebates are capped at the monthly limit. |

## How international ATM withdrawal fees are calculated
- Calculation: The fee equals the greater of:
  - 3% of the cash withdrawal amount, or
  - $5.00 (minimum)
- Threshold for the minimum to apply: The minimum applies when the withdrawal amount is less than or equal to $5.00 divided by 3%.

## When fees can combine
- If you use an international ATM that is also out‑of‑network, both the $2.50 out‑of‑network fee and the international withdrawal fee of 3% (minimum $5.00) can apply.
- ATM operator surcharges, if any, are in addition to the above.

## Monthly rebate details
- Rho rebates up to $10 in out‑of‑network ATM fees per calendar month.
- The monthly cap is the maximum total rebated; fees above this amount are your responsibility after the cap is reached.

## Tips to minimize ATM costs
- Use Rho ATMs whenever possible to avoid the out‑of‑network fee of $2.50.
- For international cash needs, consider making larger, less frequent withdrawals to reduce the impact of the $5.00 minimum relative to the withdrawal amount.
- Always review any on‑screen ATM operator surcharge disclosures before completing a transaction.

10. International ATM withdrawals for Blue Account
   ID: doc_checking_accounts_blue_account_012
   Score: 17.7662
   Content: ## Fee for international ATM withdrawals

- For ATM withdrawals made in a foreign currency, you are charged 3% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum fee of $5.00 per withdrawal.
- The fee is calculated on the U.S. dollar equivalent of the cash dispensed and is applied per transaction.

### Quick formula
Fee = the greater of:
- 3% of the withdrawal amount, or
- $5.00

## Daily ATM withdrawal limit

Your Blue Account debit card has a daily ATM withdrawal limit of $500. This limit applies to all ATM withdrawals combined (domestic and international) within a 24-hour period.

## Examples

The following examples assume the ATM dispenses local currency and the final transaction amount is converted to the U.S. dollar equivalent for fee calculation.

| Withdrawal (USD equivalent) | Percentage fee at 3% | Minimum applies? | Fee charged |
|---|---:|:--:|---:|
| $40 | $1.20 | Yes | $5.00 |
| $200 | $6.00 | No | $6.00 |
| $1,000 | $30.00 | No | $30.00 |

Tip: Because a $5.00 minimum applies to each transaction, making fewer, larger withdrawals can reduce total fees compared with multiple small withdrawals.

## How the fee appears

- The fee posts when the withdrawal settles and appears as a separate line item on your account history and statement.
- The ATM owner or network may charge its own fee at the machine. Those third‑party fees are separate and in addition to the amounts described above.

## Using international ATMs effectively

- At the ATM, choose to be charged in the local currency rather than converting at the terminal. This generally helps you avoid extra conversion costs set by the ATM provider.
- Verify the total amount before confirming the withdrawal and save the receipt.
- If an ATM displays a message about an additional operator fee, you can cancel and try another nearby bank-operated machine to potentially avoid or reduce those charges.
- If a transaction is declined after cash is not dispensed, do not retry repeatedly at the same machine; locate a different ATM.

4. Linked Checking Account APY Boost: Selection Policy
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_046
   Score: 23.4147
   Content: ## Multiple Checking Account APY Boost Selection Policy

When a customer holds multiple Rho-Bank checking accounts that each provide an APY boost on their savings account, the boosts do NOT stack. Only the highest applicable checking account APY boost is applied to the customer's savings account.

### How it works

1. The system identifies all active Rho-Bank checking accounts linked to the customer's profile.
2. For each checking account, the corresponding APY boost for the savings account type is determined.
3. Only the HIGHEST checking account APY boost is applied to the savings account.
4. Other checking account boosts are not added on top.

### Example

If a customer with a Gold Savings Account holds:
- Green Account (checking): +0.75% APY boost
- Purple Account (checking): +0.1% APY boost

The customer receives only the Green Account boost of +0.75% (the highest), not the sum of both.

### Important distinctions

- Checking account APY boosts do NOT stack with each other.
- However, checking account APY boosts DO stack with other types of bonuses, such as:
  - Credit card APY bonuses (only highest credit card bonus applies)
  - Relationship bonuses for holding multiple Rho-Bank products
  - Account tier bonuses

### Why this policy exists

This policy ensures that customers receive a meaningful benefit for holding premium checking accounts while maintaining sustainable interest rates across the product portfolio.

### Agent Responsibility

When investigating interest discrepancies for customers with multiple checking accounts, agents must:
1. Identify all checking accounts the customer holds
2. Determine which checking account provides the highest APY boost for the savings account type
3. Verify that the system is applying the highest boost, not a lower one
4. If the system selected the wrong checking account, calculate the correct APY and apply an interest correction

   Score: 17.2359
   Content: ## Scope and Focus

Procedure for opening personal savings accounts. Eligibility requirements: 1) Customer must be verified, 2) Customer must already have at least one active Rho-Bank checking account, 3) Cannot have more than 5 personal savings accounts, 4) Must not have any accounts in collections or with negative balances, 5) Must have held their checking account for at least 14 days. Steps: 1) Verify customer identity, 2) Check eligibility requirements, 3) Confirm account selection with customer, 4) Use open_bank_account_4821 to open the account (note: account_class must use the full official name ending with 'Account', e.g., 'Silver Plus Account', 'Gold Account'), 5) Ask the customer if they would like you to transfer the opening deposit from their checking account now. If yes, use transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291 to transfer the required amount. If no, inform them they have 30 days to fund the account (via internal transfer or external deposit) or the account will be closed.

## Eligibility Requirements (Internal Checklist)

Confirm all of the following before proceeding:
- Customer identity is verified in our systems.
- Customer has at least one active Rho-Bank checking account.
- Customer currently holds fewer than 5 personal savings accounts.
- Customer has no accounts in collections and no negative balances.
- The customer’s checking account tenure is at least 14 days.

Do not proceed if any item above is not met.

## Step-by-Step Procedure

1) Verify identity
- Authenticate the customer and confirm identity verification status on file.

2) Check eligibility
- Confirm an active checking account exists and meets the 14-day tenure requirement.
- Count existing personal savings accounts; ensure the customer is below the 5 limit.
- Review account status; there must be no collections activity and no negative balances.

3) Confirm account selection
- Discuss available personal savings account options with the customer.
- Capture the exact account_class string. It must be the full official name ending with “Account” (for example, “Silver Plus Account”, “Gold Account”).

4) Open the savings account (agent action)
- Use the open_bank_account_4821 tool with account_type set to 'savings' and the confirmed account_class.

5) Arrange opening deposit
- Ask the customer if they want you to transfer the opening deposit from their checking account now.
  - If yes: use transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291 to transfer the required amount from the customer’s checking account to the newly opened savings account.
  - If no: inform the customer they have 30 days to fund the account (via internal transfer or external deposit) or the account will be closed.

6) Confirm completion
- Provide the new account details and confirm the funding status or the funding deadline.

## Agent Tool Usage (Internal Only)

The AGENT calls these tools directly to perform actions on behalf of the customer. Do not ask the customer to call tools or provide tool parameters.

- Tool: open_bank_account_4821(user_id, account_type, account_class)
  - When to call: After steps 1–3, once eligibility is confirmed and the customer has selected an account_class.
  - How to set parameters:
    - user_id: the authenticated customer’s user identifier.
    - account_type: 'savings' for personal savings accounts.
    - account_class: the full official account name ending with 'Account' exactly as confirmed with the customer.
  - Expected outcome: Creates a new personal savings account for the customer.

- Tool: transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291(source_account_id, destination_account_id, amount)
  - When to call: In step 5, only if the customer authorizes an immediate transfer for the opening deposit.
  - How to set parameters:
    - source_account_id: the customer's Rho-Bank checking account to be debited.
    - destination_account_id: the newly opened personal savings account to be credited.
    - amount: the required opening deposit amount confirmed with the customer.
  - Expected outcome: Moves funds from checking to savings to complete the opening deposit.

## Decision Points and Handling

- Exceeds savings account limit: If the customer already has 5 personal savings accounts, do not open a new one. Inform the customer they have reached the maximum.
- Insufficient checking tenure: If the checking account has been open fewer than 14 days, advise the customer when they will become eligible.
- Collections or negative balances: Resolve these issues first; do not proceed until all accounts are in good standing.
- Customer defers funding: Clearly communicate the 30-day funding window and the consequence of closure if unfunded. Document the acknowledgment in the interaction notes.
